newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bank offers China's first forex trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bank offers China's first forex trading.

text.p: A bank in Shanghai will offer China's first foreign exchange trading by telephone from January 2, the Liberation Daily reported on Saturday.

Customers with foreign exchange accounts at the Bank of Communications will be able to call in orders from anywhere in China, with a minimum order of $300, and can trade in nine currencies -- Canadian, Australian, U.S. and Hong Kong dollars, Japanese yen, German marks, sterling and Swiss and French francs, it said.
The bank will only accept orders for spot transactions and deals could be completed as quickly as 30 seconds, it said.
Customers who phone in on lines equipped with fax machines will be able to get a record of the transaction sent to them by fax, it said.
The service will be available during day-time business hours from January 2 and will be extended to evening hours from March 1, the newspaper said but gave no more details.
